# Agent Harness Capabilities and an Isolated Trial Setup

Last revised: 2026-11-05

This compares six agent harnesses (Hermes Agent, OpenHands, opencode, Goose,
Codex CLI, Claude Code) and asks how to try one with an easy interface and real
isolation, on a low-power laptop that already runs NVIDIA OpenShell sandboxes or
on a home k3s cluster.

**Short answer:** use the laptop. Run Hermes inside an OpenShell sandbox and
drive it through its OpenAI-compatible API server with Open WebUI. Leave the
Telegram gateway off. k3s adds cluster blast radius without adding an isolation
layer, and only OpenHands was found shipping an official Kubernetes
deployment. The
recommendation is inference from the cited evidence; none of it was run.

## Key tables

### Interfaces: is auth on by default?

| Interface | Auth default | Cite |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes API server (+ Open WebUI) | Key required, even on 127.0.0.1:8642 | [6] |
| Claude Code Remote Control | claude.ai login, outbound-only, no API keys | [110] |
| Goose `goose serve` | Secret required unless `--dangerously-unauthenticated` | [83] |
| opencode `serve` / `web` | Off ("unsecured") unless password set | [61] |
| Codex app-server WebSocket | Off on non-loopback; "experimental and unsupported" | [94] |
| OpenHands Agent Canvas | "unauthenticated, single-tenant" | [45] |
| Hermes Telegram gateway | Disputed: docs deny-by-default vs open fail-open issue | [8][17] |

### Isolation: what each harness brings

| Harness | Own OS sandbox | Cite |
|---|---|---|
| Hermes | Default backend has "no isolation"; optional Docker backend | [4] |
| OpenHands | Docker sandbox; open rootless-Podman issues, no merged Podman backend | [51][53][54][55] |
| opencode | None documented (permission rules, mostly "allow") | [62] |
| Goose | None documented (Autonomous mode by default) | [79] |
| Codex CLI | bubblewrap + seccomp; fails nested under Ubuntu AppArmor | [96][98] |
| Claude Code | bubblewrap Bash sandbox; MCP and hooks run unconstrained | [113][114] |

### Laptop vs k3s

| | Laptop (OpenShell, rootless Podman) | k3s |
|---|---|---|
| OpenShell support | Podman "Supported for rootless local and workstation workflows" [26] | Helm chart "Experimental" [28]; matrix says "Supported" [26] |
| k3s named | n/a | No [27][28][34] |
| Official harness deployment | Install inside sandbox | OpenHands chart only (in fetched sources), unauthenticated [45] |
| Extra isolation | None beyond containers | None without gVisor/Kata [35] |

## Decision framework

1. **Laptop first.** It already has a supported OpenShell driver [26]. Choose
   k3s only for always-on uptime, and add gVisor or Kata if you do [35].
2. **Hermes + API server + Open WebUI** for the easy interface. The key is
   required by default [6]. Reach it by port-forward or SSH tunnel [22]. Run
   `terminal.backend: local` so OpenShell is the boundary [4].
3. **Keep chat gateways off.** The Telegram default is disputed [8][17], and it
   was a botnet's command channel [128].
4. **Assume the sandbox leaks its credentials.** Repo-borne RCE exposed Hermes
   provider keys [122]. Use a dedicated, spend-limited provider key. Claude
   subscriptions are restricted in third-party harnesses [105].
5. **Zero-setup comparison:** Claude Code Remote Control from the existing
   sandbox. It is outbound-only and authenticated [110]. That it works in this
   sandbox is untested inference.

## Caveats

- Discovery used one search engine (Yahoo). The other engines were blocking the
  sandbox's IP. See [analysis.md § Limitations](analysis.md#limitations).
- Every harness had a high or critical CVE in 2025–2026. See
  [references/isolation-k3s-security.md](references/isolation-k3s-security.md).
